physiology.note: The 'medical' physiology model (M10.1), on top of core/wounds.json physiology (owner clock of 2026-11-11, unchanged). Research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only. Tension pneumothorax: 3-4 % of the fatally wounded, 15 of 26 lived long enough to reach a medic (J Trauma 2006, medium); the chance per penetrating chest wound (0.15), onset 5-30 min and death 10 min after onset are game values. Head injury: some conscious head wounds pass out after a lucid interval of 2-30 min (game values). Broken bones: 35 % of limb wounds of severity 0.25 or more (game value). Burns lose plasma (Parkland formula: about 4 ml per kg per % body surface per day; 0.0003 l/s per unit of burn severity, game value). Fluids: 500 ml run in over 10 min, 70 % of it counts as circulating volume (game value). Hypothermia: about twice the mortality, below 32 C core almost always fatal in trauma (Hypothermia Prevention CPG 2012, medium); a man in shock at 15 C air cools about 2 C an hour, wet x2, wind up to x1.5, aboard x0.3, wrapped x0.2 (game values); below 35 C clotting is twice as slow and every degree lowers the lethal blood loss by 3 points; out below 31 C, dead at 28 C. Tourniquet clock: no limb lost within 2 h (Kragh et al., J Trauma 2008, medium); amputation chance rising to 0.5 at 6 h and 0.9 at 10 h (extrapolation, low; owner to review).

levels.note: Medical jobs (owner 2026-11-14): first responder (Einsatzersthelfer B, strelok-sanitar), medic (Sanitaeter), stretcher bearer (riflemen tasked by the platoon leader: buddy-level skill), ambulance crew (medic level). A role may narrow what it is trained for (roles.json medical.interventions; owner Q-1b).

interventions.note: Research 2026-11-14 (search extracts only): experienced appliers about 25 s, inexperienced 28-38 s (JSOM 2025); self-application 3-8 s slower and 9-22 % less effective (Am J Transl Res 2021, PMC8290695); IDF field data 22 % failed to occlude, non-medical personnel fail often. Self-aid succeeds at the buddy chance times selfFactor. Care under fire: the only treatment allowed (TCCC), 1.3x slower (game value). Picks within the ranges are game values.
Re-check and tighten a tourniquet: tourniquets lose pressure within about 2 minutes of being applied, non-elastic straps especially (JSOM 2020, search extract). Time and success are game values.
Emergency (Israeli) bandage, Verbandpaeckchen, IPP-1. No measured time found in search extracts; times, success and the effect (bleeding x0.15) are game values.

Pack with haemostatic gauze (up to about 90 s) then hold pressure 3 minutes (JEMS 'Wound packing essentials', TCCC neck-wound guidance; search extracts). About 90 % haemostasis where haemostatic gauze is used (JEMS). Packing time and the success picks are game values.
Recovery position, sitting up, chin lift. No timing found; game values.
Nasopharyngeal airway. TCCC skill sheets list the steps, no time; Einsatzersthelfer B trains airway care (bundeswehr.de, search extract). Times and success are game values.
Vented chest seal. TCCC module 8 lists steps, no time. A tension pneumothorax may still develop and then needs decompression. Game values.

Failure 58 % in one series (J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2012), 3.2 cm catheters fail up to 65 %, about 80 % success with 5 cm catheters (reviews; search extracts). Einsatzersthelfer B trains airway relief (owner Q-1b: per national training). Times are game values.

IV versus IO 77 vs 83 s median (Cureus 2025 via ivteam.com); IV first attempt 46 % in hypovolaemic shock against IO 100 % (search extracts). stressFactor here stands for 'in shock'. Picks are game values.
FAST1 sternal 62-67 s (Hartholt 2010); FAST1 72-73 %, EZ-IO 87 % first-attempt success (field trial; search extracts). Picks are game values.
Hang a 500 ml bag on an access already placed: the time is connecting it; it then runs in over about 10 minutes (physiology fluidLps). TCCC prefers blood, which a platoon does not carry. Game values.
TCCC tablet pack (meloxicam and paracetamol), onset reassessed at 15 minutes (Ranger Medic Handbook 2025; search extract). Time and the relief are game values.
Opioid autoinjector or syringe tube (the Russian kit holds a promedol syringe tube, nordsint.org; fentanyl lozenge in TCCC). Time and relief are game values.
Ketamine 0.5 mg/kg IM or IN, repeat every 30-60 min (Ranger Medic Handbook 2025, search extract). Medics only. Time and relief are game values.
Rescue blanket or hypothermia prevention kit; hypothermic casualties have about twice the mortality (Hypothermia Prevention CPG 2012, search extract). No time found; game values.
SAM or improvised splint. Nothing found in search extracts; game values.
Replace a tourniquet with a pressure dressing (TCCC; medics only, within 2 hours). Game values.

carry.note: Walking wounded, unaided: about 60 % of a walk (leg wounds slow him further through the wound effects). Game value.
Arm over a comrade's shoulder. Game values.

One-man drag by the vest handle: 110 kg over 20 m in about 27 s by fit civilians (0.74 m/s); British Army standard 110 kg 20 m within 35 s (Vine et al., Applied Ergonomics 2023). A soldier in kit is about 105 kg. Endurance and rest are game values.
Two-person drag studied by Vine et al. 2023 (times not in the extract). Game values.
Fireman's carry: exposes both men upright (TCCC and US manuals advise a drag under fire). Speed and endurance are game values.
Two-man seat or fore-and-aft carry; two-person hand carry of a litter lasts about 3 minutes to exhaustion (1994 stretcher study, search extract). Game values.

Four-man litter: 4.8 km/h on a treadmill (1.33 m/s), proposed 1.0 m/s over ground; continuous carry up to about 5 minutes with harness (stretcher studies, search extracts); 30-60 s to unfold and load. Game values.

carrying.note: M10.4a carrying parties (game values, none published): carriers gather within reachM of the casualty before they set off; a party whose carrier is pinned or at holdSuppression or more takes cover with the casualty (owner M10-2 Q-2f) and goes on after resumeQuietS quiet; carriers fire only at an enemy within selfDefenceM (self-defence, owner); massRefKg: the casualty mass the carry speeds are for (a soldier in kit, about 105 kg: Vine et al. 2023 used 110 kg).

vehicleLoading.note: M10.4b casualties into and out of vehicles (game values, none published; search extracts only say a stretcher in an infantry carrier takes the room of several seated men). fetchM: a unit getting into its vehicle carries its wounded who cannot walk from up to this far (to the nearest exit, as a carrying party) before it drives off; lyingSeats: in a vehicle without an ambulance layout a man lying down takes this many passenger seats (1: he is laid across the floor and the bench in the room of his own seat, so a full squad still takes its wounded; with 2, a full Puma squad could not take one of its own lying down — decided without the owner, low); lyingShock: a casualty lies (rather than sits) when he is unconscious or his shock is at this or more (as triage's immediateShock). An ambulance uses its own layouts (lying, sitting and outside places, vehicles.json `ambulance`).

nest.note: M10.5 Verwundetennest (platoon casualty collection point; Bundeswehr reports name a company Verwundetensammelpunkt, search extracts only; the platoon term is the owner's). Game values, none published: the nest is sited backM 150 m behind the platoon's centre, away from the enemy its men know (else toward the nearest map edge), within minBackM-maxBackM, at the spot within searchM that is hidden (lying) from that enemy, open ground a wheeled vehicle can reach from that edge; a casualty within arriveM is at the nest. Checked every checkS: a known enemy within threatM of a nest the player did not place moves it; an empty nest more than driftM from the platoon's centre follows it. The platoon leader tasks bearers (riflemen, owner M10-2 Q-2e): bearers men per casualty who cannot walk (one alone, a fireman's carry, when no second man is free), at most maxParties parties per platoon at once, never leaving a squad with fewer than minFitLeft fit men; walking wounded walk there themselves. A man at the nest fit to fight again goes back to his squad. The platoon's best-trained medical man (DE the Sanitaeter, RU the rifleman-medic) goes to the nest when it is within medicReachM, to triage again and give the care he alone can.

evacuation.note: M10.6a ambulance runs. delayMinS-delayMaxS 600-900 s: the owner's answer (M10-3 Q-6: 10-15 min plus the drive) for an ambulance called from the company or battalion behind; research extracts only give the 10-1-2 rule (Role 1 within 60 min) and 'protected ambulance on request', no figure for the call itself. Game values, none published (decided without the owner, low): it drives at the 'walk' pace (the wheeled 'wdrive-slow' pace, 30 % of its top speed: about 30 km/h for the Boxer, 24 km/h for the BMM; at the 'run' pace, 70 %, hulls ran into hedges at route corners in the lab), and so does nearPace near the nest (a hull's look-ahead for men in its way must not reach the men lying there); it stops standM 15 m short of the Verwundetennest (not on top of the men lying there), or where its way first comes within 65 m of the nest, or where the ground holds it up within 80 m; its crew fetches each casualty on a litter at carryMps 1.0 m/s (the two-man carry's speed) each way plus loadSecondsExtra 20 s (onto the litter) and the hull's loadCasualtySeconds (lifting him in), T1 first; it leaves when full, or waitS 120 s after the last man came aboard with nobody else on the way to the nest, at most maxStayS 600 s after it arrived; it is off the map within edgeM 20 m of its entry point; a route not found is tried again after retryS 30 s; requestAt: an automatic call goes out once this many casualties are waiting at the nest (1).

chain.note: Bundeswehr 10-1-2 rule: life-saving bleeding control and airway within 10 minutes, a doctor (Role 1) within 60 minutes, surgery within 2 hours (bundeswehr.de 'Rettungskette', search extract).

protection.note: Law: medical personnel, transports and men hors de combat are protected while they commit no acts harmful to the enemy (CIHL rules 25, 29, 47; GC I art. 19, 21, 22, 24). The numbers are game values (none published): an emblem on a vehicle recognised to about 300 m by eye and 800 m with optics, an armband to 50 m / 150 m, x0.3 in smoke or at night; a deliberate breach 1 % per decision, x3 after own losses, x2 for poor discipline, x2 when panicked (owner answer 5: from unit quality, stress and losses only, never from faction); a medic who fights loses protection for 120 s after his last shot.

triage.note: Triage (M10.3b). Categories as in NATO practice and the Bundeswehr's Sichtungskategorien: T1 immediate (red, SK I), T2 delayed (yellow, SK II), T3 minimal (green, SK III); T4 expectant (blue, SK IV) is a mass-casualty category a platoon does not assign and is left out (search extracts only: medium for the scheme, low for the rest). The true category: T1 when he needs one of immediateTreats (massive bleeding, airway, breathing; MARCH) or his shock is at immediateShock or more or his consciousness below immediateConsciousness; T2 when he cannot walk or needs any other care; T3 otherwise (walking wounded). The man who treats him (a comrade, first responder or medic; not himself) tags him at his first treatment; a man of higher training, or anyone once the tag is retriageS old, tags him again. A tag is wrong (one category off) with errorChance by training, plus underFireAdd under fire (SPEC 9.1: sometimes wrong). The error chances and thresholds are game values.

care.note: How care is given (M10.2, game values unless said). Order: the MARCH sequence of TCCC tactical field care (massive bleeding, airway, respiration, circulation, hypothermia; then pain and splints; deployedmedicine.com, search extracts: medium for the sequence, low for the rest). A man treats himself (self-aid) when he can; otherwise the nearest comrade of his side within buddyReachM (3 m, roadmap plan) does it. Under fire (own suppression at least underFireSuppression, or his unit fired on within underFireSeconds) only interventions marked underFire (the tourniquet; TCCC care under fire). A bleed is life-threatening when it is too large to clot by itself (core/wounds.json clotBelowLps). Each intervention at most maxAttempts times on one wound; success and time also depend on the man's own medical skill: x (1 + skillK x (skill - skillRef)). Pain is treated at painTreatAt or more, once. Junctional bleeds (wound packing): the zones listed. Re-checking and converting a tourniquet come with the medic (M10.5). Care under fire (M10.3b; TCCC: return fire, move the casualty to cover, a tourniquet): a helper beside a casualty who lies where the enemy can see him sends him to the nearest spot hidden from that enemy within dragSearchM (a way at most dragMaxM long), after a tourniquet if one is needed: a casualty who can walk goes there himself, one who cannot is dragged there (core carry 'drag': speed); a comrade of his unit throws smoke to screen it if he has a grenade. Lying there, care is judged under fire on the helper's own suppression only (the cover is what makes tactical field care possible). The radio calls 'Medic!' and 'Man down, treating' come at most once each per radioCooldownS per unit. Search radius, way and cooldown: game values.

carers.note: Who goes to a casualty further away than buddy reach (M10.3a; game values, no public source for the numbers). A casualty looks urgent (T1) when he needs care for one of urgentTreats (massive bleeding, airway, breathing, shock; MARCH). An urgent casualty gets a first responder or medic of his platoon within responderReachM (his own squad's first; owner Q-1c: one Einsatzersthelfer B per Gruppe, a Sanitaeter in the Zug HQ; one rifleman-medic per Russian platoon) and also a willing comrade; any other casualty a willing comrade, else a free first responder. At most the first responder plus comradesPerCasualty comrade per casualty (owner Q-2a: in contact, the first responder plus at most one comrade). Willingness = doctrine casualtyCarePriority x behaviourK (by his behaviour; others 0) x morale x (1 - suppressionK x suppression) x otherUnitK (not his own squad) x exposedK (the casualty under fire) x responderK (first responders and medics: it is their job); willing at willingAt or more. Squad and platoon leaders do not leave their men. A comrade carer goes back once a first responder is beside the casualty. A carer gives up after timeoutS.

down.note: Men down (owner request 2026-11-15; game values, low). A man who has gone down is to his comrades 'down, state unknown' until one of them is beside him and checks him (checkS 5 s: responsiveness, breathing; TCCC assessment, search extracts only); until then they come to him and drag him to cover like any casualty, though he may be dead. A comrade who finds him dead takes his identity tag (factions/<id>/doctrine.json identityTag) in tagS 8 s, only with his own suppression below tagSuppression, not cowering, and no rounds cracking past him for tagQuietS 20 s; a confirmed dead man whose tag is still on him is fetched by a willing comrade when it is that quiet. A conscious casualty who cannot walk but can use his arms crawls (the crawl pace times his wound impairment) to the nearest spot hidden from the enemy within crawlSearchM 10 m by a way at most crawlMaxM 15 m, looked at every crawlLookS 4 s while he is under fire for care, unless a carer of his is within crawlCarerNearM 15 m.
